text:
renee cole: hey team, first-week head-scratcher. I set `network_mode: host` on the api service because I wanted the container to hit my host postgres at localhost:5432, but now the api container can't resolve the `db` service name and fails with `getaddrinfo: Name or service not known`. I'm on mac (Ventura) using Docker Desktop.

renee cole: compose snippet I added (naive):
```yaml
services:
  api:
    build: .
    network_mode: host
  db:
    image: postgres:14
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pass
```

tom harper: welcome renee  short version: `network_mode: host` behaves differently on macOS. Docker Desktop runs containers in a lightweight VM, so host networking doesn't give you the same Linux host network. It also removes the user-defined network where service name DNS works, so `db` won't be resolvable. On mac, host mode is effectively unsupported for service-name DNS.

anya petrov: yep. two concrete fixes: 1) remove `network_mode: host` and rely on compose networking (service names like `db:5432`), or 2) if you need container to talk to a DB running on your host machine, use the docker-for-mac special DNS name `host.docker.internal:5432` and keep normal networks. Example: `DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pass@host.docker.internal:5432/app_dev` when running inside container.

tom harper: also, for db in compose you can expose the port and keep service name for inter-container comms. Eg:
```yaml
  db:
    image: postgres:14
    ports:
      - "5432:5432" # host access
```
Then other containers connect to `db:5432` and host can connect to localhost:5432. Avoid `network_mode: host` unless you know the portability tradeoffs.

renee cole: that makes sense. I actually wanted to iterate quickly by running the web on my host while db is containerized, so I thought host mode was easiest. What's the recommended dev workflow?

anya petrov: common patterns: a) run all services in compose and iterate inside containers for parity, b) run db in compose and run app on host but point the host app at `localhost:5432` (make sure ports are mapped and no host postgres colliding), c) if running app in container but need to reach a host service, use `host.docker.internal`. For local iteration, we usually run the web inside the container to avoid host vs container differences.

tom harper: quick debugging tips: `docker compose ps` shows running services; `docker compose logs db` shows bind/start errors; `docker compose exec api ping -c1 db` checks DNS; `docker compose exec api getent hosts db` if available. Also `docker compose config` prints resolved networks and `docker network ls`/`docker network inspect <name>` help diagnose separate networks.

renee cole: I removed `network_mode`, added `ports: - "5432:5432"` and set my host app's DATABASE_URL to `postgres://postgres:pass@localhost:5432/app_dev`. The containerized api connects to `db:5432` fine when I run it in compose.

anya petrov: nice. small note: exposing ports can cause collisions if you have a host postgres (brew). If you have host postgres running, either stop it (`brew services stop postgres`) or pick a different host port like `"15432:5432"` and point host app to `localhost:15432`. For cross-container comms, don't rely on host ports  use service names instead.

infra-bot: Dev tip: onboarding guide updated with a short section "Avoid network_mode: host on macOS" and examples for host.docker.internal + port remapping. See https://redwood.internal/devenv/networking.

renee cole: thanks everyone  removing `network_mode` fixed the service name resolution and my workflow is smooth now. I'll add a note to the repo README about host.docker.internal and port collisions. :raised_hands:
